craft_notes: Sthāyin: entitlement-stated (FIRST-VERSE of the āhnika-block; plain injunctive diction, end-weighted; owner verdict flagged before treating as voice). Sanskrit: svabhyastajñāninaṃ...abhiṣiñcet...na anyaḥ → L4 keeps consecrate-entitle-no-other arc. Rows: row 3 (entitles→no-other). Close: absent (knowing-absent as closer). Rejected: 'initiate' for consecrate — kept consecrate (abhiṣeka as pouring-over); 'sādhaka/ācārya terms' — kept practitioner/teacher (plain English house diction).

lines: Consecrate the knowing-practised — practitioner or teacher be he;
marks or markless, knowing alone entitles —
to practising, to grace-giving. No other:
not even the anointed, if knowing is absent.
l4.sanskrit_cite: svabhyastajñāninaṃ sādhakatve gurutve vā abhiṣiñcet yataḥ sarvalakṣaṇahīno 'pi jñānavān eva sādhakatve anugrahakaraṇe ca adhikṛtaḥ na anyaḥ abhiṣikto 'pi

reads_against.argmap: Who is to be consecrated, and why? → Entitlement follows knowledge, not marks and not prior consecration: the markless knower alone is fit for practitionerhood or guruhood.
c1_essence: Consecrate the practiced knower as practitioner or teacher: knowing alone entitles; marks or prior consecration do not.
reads_against.c1_rasa: śānta with vidhi weight (quiescence carrying injunction)
